summary: Friedrich Delitzsch worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch, Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Hermann Brockhaus, Georg Curtius, and August Dillmann. He later held posts at the universities of Breslau (~1893–1899) and Berlin (~1899–1920).
Friedrich Ernst August Krause was a sinologist who studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin. He later held a post at the University of Heidelberg from circa 1925 to 1940.

Friedrich Haag studied at Zurich (Dr. phil. and Habilitation) under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, as well as Göttingen and Berlin. He taught at Zurich (1873–1884), directed schools in Schaffhausen and Burgdorf, and became professor of classical philology at the University of Bern (1891–1906).

Friedrich Heiler was a religious studies scholar who completed his dissertation at the University of Munich (~1912–1917), where he taught in 1918. He took up a post at the University of Marburg in 1920 and directed the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

Friedrich Heinrich Hugo Windischmann studied at Bonn under Christian Lassen, Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel, and at Munich. He held professorships at the Lyzeum Freising and Munich (1838–1839) before serving as General Vicar in Munich and Freising (~1846–1861).

Friedrich Hirth was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald (dissertation ~1868–1869). He served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) and held the Dean Lung Professorship of Chinese at Columbia University from 1902.

Friedrich Leo worked in linguistics, studying at Bonn under Hermann Usener and at Göttingen. He held academic posts at Bonn (1877–1881), Kiel (1881–1883), Rostock (1883–1888), Strasbourg (1888–1889), and the University of Göttingen (1889–1914).

Friedrich Majer was an indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder, later serving as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena.

Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and under Brockhaus, Burnouf, Bopp, Schelling, and Wilson. He spent his career at the University of Oxford, becoming professor of comparative philology in 1868.

Friedrich Müller specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Vienna, Göttingen, and Tübingen under Anton Boller. After posts at the Vienna University Library and Austrian National Library, he served as Privatdozent (1858–1866) and Professor (from 1869) at the University of Vienna.

Friedrich Nietzsche was a philosopher and linguist who studied at the University of Bonn and the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Ritschl. He served on the faculty at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

Friedrich Otto Schrader was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a Dr. theol. from the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1902). He served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916) and became a professor at Kiel University in 1921.

Friedrich Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Halle (~1829–1833), Breslau (1834), Bonn (1839), and the University of Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Friedrich Rosen studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1826). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London (~1828–1837) and Professor of Oriental Literature at the University of London (1834).

Friedrich Rückert was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Würzburg and Heidelberg, and under Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at Erlangen (1826) and Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying at Göttingen and Leipzig under Heyne, Hamilton, and de Chézy. He held posts at Jena (1800), the University of Cologne and École Centrale de Cologne (1804–1806), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich Schleiermacher was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1790). He held a post at Halle-Wittenberg (~1804–1807) and a chair at the University of Berlin from circa 1810 to 1834.
Friedrich Schrader was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885–1889), completing his dissertation under Richard Pischel.

Friedrich Weller worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing his doctorate and habilitation at Leipzig under August Conrady. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig, holding the chair of Indian philology from 1938 to 1958.

Friedrich Wilhelm is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Paul Thieme and completed his promotion at Munich (~1951–1956). He spent his career at the University of Munich, serving as professor from 1969 to 1998.
